pages.title: AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill 2026 — Amaravati declared capital

facts.text: Change: "there shall be a new capital" → "Amaravati shall be the new capital"
facts.head: News

facts.text: Amaravati defined as the area notified under the AP Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) Act, 2014
facts.head: News

facts.text: Retrospective effect: from 2 June 2024
facts.head: News

facts.text: AP Legislative Assembly resolution requesting the amendment: 28 March 2026 — reflects cooperative federalism
facts.head: News

facts.text: AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 — enacted under Article 3; created Telangana
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Section 5: Hyderabad = common capital for not more than 10 years from 2 June 2014 (i.e., till 2024)
facts.head: Background

facts.text: ⚠ The 2014 Act did not name Amaravati or any city as capital — only said a new capital would be established
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Parliament passed the Bill — Amaravati = sole and permanent capital; broad support except YSR Congress Party (had pushed three-capital model)
facts.head: Parliament passage and history

facts.text: 2019: then govt proposed three capitals (executive, legislative, judicial functions split)
facts.head: Parliament passage and history

facts.text: 2022: AP High Court ruled the State lacked legislative competence to shift the capital
facts.head: Parliament passage and history

facts.text: Amendment is to Section 5 of the 2014 Act
facts.head: Parliament passage and history

facts.text: Location: banks of Krishna River, between Vijayawada and Guntur
facts.head: Amaravati capital project

facts.text: Planned area: ~217 sq. km; developed via Land Pooling Scheme (farmers get developed plots + compensation)

facts.text: Implementing body: APCRDA; master plan with Surbana Jurong (Singapore)
facts.head: Amaravati capital project

facts.text: President Droupadi Murmu granted assent → AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 — inserts "at Amaravati" in Section 5
facts.head: Presidential assent and constitutional angle

facts.text: Three-capital model (post-2019): Visakhapatnam (executive), Amaravati (legislative), Kurnool (judicial) — via AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020; ⚠ repealed in 2021, judicial capital never operationalised
facts.head: Presidential assent and constitutional angle

facts.text: 2022 HC: State cannot arbitrarily change capital — legitimate expectation of Land Pooling farmers; rule of law; judicial review under Articles 32 & 226
facts.head: Presidential assent and constitutional angle

facts.text: ⚠ The Constitution does not specify how a State capital is determined — statutory law fills the gap
facts.head: Presidential assent and constitutional angle

facts.text: APCRDA Act, 2014: special planning body — Town Planning Schemes, Betterment Charges; overriding powers over Gram Panchayats in capital region
facts.head: Presidential assent and constitutional angle
